skill.name: data-structure-protocol
skill.description: Build and maintain a persistent codebase graph that records entities, dependencies, public APIs, and reasons for each connection.
skill.summary: Map code structure once, then query and update it across coding tasks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Two linked findings confirm one supply-chain risk: an unpinned Python CLI is downloaded from a mutable branch and later executed. The other 53 findings are safe Markdown, fixed local examples, metadata, or documentation links. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The setup downloads executable Python from an unpinned main-branch URL without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed CLI or pin its URL to an immutable commit, publish a SHA-256 checksum, and verify it before execution.

content.value_statement: Large repositories force coding agents to rediscover structure during every task. DSP stores a queryable dependency graph with stable identities and explicit connection reasons.
actual_capabilities: Initializes a plain-text DSP graph for a project.
Assigns stable identifiers to files, artifacts, and exported functions.
Records imports, public exports, and reasons for each dependency.
Searches entities by description or source path.
Traces parents, children, recipients, and paths between entities.
Detects dependency cycles, orphaned entities, and graph statistics.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10 or later and a separate DSP CLI script.
Bootstrap maps reachable imports and may miss disconnected project files.
Graph accuracy depends on updates after structural code changes.
External dependency internals and runtime behavior are not analyzed.

use_cases.title: Orient New Contributors
use_cases.description: Query the graph to locate modules, public APIs, and dependency reasons before changing unfamiliar code.

use_cases.title: Plan Safe Refactors
use_cases.description: Trace recipients and dependency paths to estimate the impact of moving modules or replacing libraries.

use_cases.title: Preserve Agent Context
use_cases.description: Maintain a persistent structural map that coding agents can reuse across separate tasks and context windows.
use_cases.target_user: Teams using Claude, Codex, or Claude Code

prompt_templates.title: Bootstrap a Project Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize DSP for {project_root}. Identify entrypoints, map reachable local imports, record public exports, and explain each dependency reason.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a first structural map for a repository.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the existing DSP graph to locate {feature}. Summarize relevant entities, dependencies, public APIs, and likely change points.
prompt_templates.scenario: Navigate an unfamiliar feature before editing code.

prompt_templates.title: Synchronize Structural Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: After implementing {change}, update DSP for every affected file, import, export, move, or deletion. Preserve all stable identifiers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep the graph aligned with a completed code change.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Dependency Replacement
prompt_templates.prompt: Before replacing {dependency}, trace every recipient and graph path. Group impacts by module and propose a staged migration with validation steps.

output_examples.input: Map the authentication service and explain its dependencies.
output: Authentication is owned by the user service module.
It imports token validation for session checks and user storage for account lookup.
Its public login operation is used by the API and administration modules.

output_examples.input: Assess the impact of replacing the utility library.
output: The utility library has five direct recipients across three modules.
Date formatting and collection helpers require separate migration paths.
Update shared services first, then validate API and reporting recipients.

output_examples.input: Update DSP after moving the payment module.
output_examples.output: The payment entity keeps its stable identifier, receives the new source path, and retains all import and recipient relationships.

best_practices: Update DSP immediately after files, imports, exports, or public purposes change.
Write short dependency reasons that explain why each connection exists.
Review DSP changes with the related code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not assign entities to local variables or private helper details.
Do not replace stable identifiers when files move or receive new names.
Do not treat the graph as a substitute for tests or runtime validation.

faq.question: What does DSP store?
faq.answer: DSP stores entities, source paths, imports, public exports, dependency reasons, and reverse recipient relationships in plain text.

faq.question: Does DSP analyze third-party package internals?
faq.answer: No. It records external packages as entities but does not traverse their internal files.

faq.question: When should the graph be updated?
faq.answer: Update it when files, imports, exports, locations, or entity purposes change.

faq.question: Does an internal implementation change require an update?
faq.answer: No update is needed when purpose, dependencies, public APIs, and file locations remain unchanged.

faq.question: Can DSP replace source review and testing?
faq.answer: No. It supports navigation and impact analysis, while source review and tests validate actual behavior.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: The documented workflow requires Python 3.10 or later and the separate DSP CLI script.
